You're welcome! I'm glad the explanation was helpful. Let's dive deeper into phantom reads.

SQL
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders WHERE order_amount BETWEEN 100 AND 200;
order_idorder_amount
10150.00
102120.00
10375.00

  • Same Query: You run the exact same SELECT statement (often a range query or a COUNT(*) over a range).

  • Different Results: The second execution of the query returns a different number of rows or includes rows that were not present in the first result set.

  • Insertion/Deletion: This difference is due to rows being inserted or deleted by another transaction that committed between your two identical queries.

  • Isolation Level: Phantom reads are a concern in isolation levels that aim for strong consistency, like REPEATABLE READ. They are not a concern in READ UNCOMMITTED (which allows even dirtier reads) or READ COMMITTED (which only guarantees that rows you actually read are committed, but doesn't prevent new rows from appearing in a range). They are prevented in SERIALIZABLE.
